question: What is a primary public health risk associated with poor health care waste management in Nigeria?

options.A: Increased rates of chronic lifestyle diseases
options.B: Transmission of blood-borne pathogens like HIV and Hepatitis
options.C: Rapid depletion of hospital pharmaceutical supplies

explanation: Improper handling of health care waste can lead to the transmission of blood-borne pathogens such as HIV, Hepatitis B, and Hepatitis C among workers and the public. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T15#GNS122_U3_T15_h1)

question: Why is health care waste management considered a fundamental nursing duty?

options.A: It is solely required for hospital accreditation
options.B: It directly supports patient safety and infection prevention
options.C: It reduces the financial cost of purchasing new equipment
options.D: It replaces the need for standard handwashing protocols

explanation: Proper waste management is tied directly to patient safety and infection prevention by reducing nosocomial infections and preventing injuries. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T15#GNS122_U3_T15_h1)

question: Which federal bodies are primarily responsible for formulating national policies on health care waste management in Nigeria?

options.A: Federal Ministry of Education and Ministry of Finance
options.B: Federal Ministry of Environment and Federal Ministry of Health
options.C: Federal Ministry of Works and Ministry of Transport
options.D: Federal Ministry of Agriculture and Ministry of Petroleum

explanation: The Federal Ministry of Environment and the Federal Ministry of Health are the key institutions that formulate national policies and guidelines for health care waste management. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T15#GNS122_U3_T15_h2)

question: What is a mandatory requirement for healthcare establishments under the National Health Care Waste Management Policy?

options.A: To export all hazardous waste to neighboring countries
options.B: To develop and implement a facility-specific waste management plan
options.C: To rely exclusively on open-air burning for disposal
options.D: To transfer waste management duties entirely to patients

explanation: National policies mandate that every healthcare establishment must develop and implement a facility-specific waste management plan to ensure compliance and safety. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T15#GNS122_U3_T15_h2)

question: What approximate percentage of total waste generated in healthcare settings is typically classified as non-hazardous general waste?
explanation: Non-hazardous general waste constitutes about 75% to 90% of the total waste generated in healthcare facilities, consisting of items like paper, packaging, and food scraps. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T15#GNS122_U3_T15_h3)

question: Which of the following falls under the category of hazardous health care waste?

options.C: Sharps such as used needles and scalpels

explanation: Sharps, including used needles and scalpels, are classified as hazardous health care waste due to the risk of puncture injuries and blood-borne pathogen transmission. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T15#GNS122_U3_T15_h3)

question: At what point in the clinical workflow should health care waste segregation take place?

options.A: At the final disposal site outside the hospital
options.B: At the exact point of generation by the healthcare worker
options.C: By the municipal waste collectors upon arrival

explanation: Segregation must occur at the exact point of generation by the healthcare worker who generated the waste to prevent contamination of general refuse. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T15#GNS122_U3_T15_h4)

question: When should waste bags and safety boxes be securely sealed and removed from the ward?

options.A: When they are completely filled to the brim
options.C: Once every week, regardless of how full they are
options.D: Only after a patient is discharged

explanation: Containers and bags should never be overloaded; they must be sealed and collected when they reach three-quarters (75%) full to prevent spills and punctures. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T15#GNS122_U3_T15_h4)

question: Why is it recommended to limit the on-site storage duration of hazardous health care waste, especially in warm climates like Nigeria?

options.A: To prevent putrefaction, vector attraction, and foul odors
options.B: To reduce the electricity bill of the facility
options.C: To ensure nurses have more storage space for linens
options.D: To comply with pharmaceutical inventory rules

explanation: Limiting storage duration prevents putrefaction, the attraction of vectors like flies and rodents, and the buildup of foul odors in warm climates. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T15#GNS122_U3_T15_h5)

question: What feature must internal trolleys used for transporting health care waste possess?

options.A: Open wire baskets for maximum ventilation
options.B: Leak-proof construction and smooth, easy-to-clean surfaces
options.C: Built-in refrigeration units for all waste types
options.D: Carpeted lining to dampen operational noise

explanation: Internal transport trolleys must be leak-proof, easy to clean, and free of sharp edges to prevent accidental spills and contamination. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T15#GNS122_U3_T15_h5)

question: What is the primary function of autoclaving in health care waste management?

options.A: To burn waste into toxic ash
options.B: To sterilize infectious waste and sharps using pressurized steam
options.C: To chemically dissolve heavy metals and plastics
options.D: To freeze pathological waste for long-term preservation

explanation: Autoclaving utilizes pressurized steam to sterilize infectious waste, rendering it biologically safe before final disposal. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T15#GNS122_U3_T15_h6)

question: Why are open dumping and uncontrolled burning of hazardous health care waste prohibited in Nigeria?

options.A: Because they are too expensive to perform regularly
options.B: Because they cause catastrophic impacts on public health and environmental safety
options.C: Because municipal collectors prefer sorting wet waste
options.D: Because incinerators require dry wood instead

explanation: Open dumping and uncontrolled burning are banned because they release toxic pollutants, spread diseases, and cause severe environmental degradation. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T15#GNS122_U3_T15_h6)

question: What is the immediate first-aid action a nurse should take after experiencing an accidental needlestick injury?

options.A: Apply a tight tourniquet above the injury site
options.B: Wash the affected site thoroughly with soap and running water
options.C: Cover the wound immediately with a tight adhesive bandage without washing
options.D: Squeeze the wound forcefully to drain out all blood

explanation: Immediate first aid for a needlestick injury involves washing the affected site thoroughly with soap and running water to remove contaminants. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T15#GNS122_U3_T15_h7)

question: Which of the following is considered a mandatory preventive occupational health requirement for nursing personnel in Nigeria?

options.C: Wearing lead aprons during all shifts
options.D: Undergoing weekly heavy metal blood screenings

explanation: Routine immunization against vaccine-preventable occupational hazards like Hepatitis B is essential for protecting healthcare workers. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T15#GNS122_U3_T15_h7)

question: What is a primary clinical responsibility of nurses regarding health care waste management?

options.A: Operating the central hospital incinerator daily
options.B: Enforcing correct waste segregation at the bedside
options.C: Transporting all waste bags to municipal landfills
options.D: Purchasing waste bins for the entire hospital

explanation: Nurses are responsible for enforcing correct waste segregation and ensuring that color-coded bins and safety boxes are properly utilized at the point of generation. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T15#GNS122_U3_T15_h8)

question: Besides direct patient care, how do nursing leaders contribute to institutional waste management?

options.A: By conducting regular safety audits and monitoring ward practices
options.C: By manufacturing chemical disinfectants in the ward
options.D: By banning all disposable medical equipment

explanation: Nursing leaders contribute by monitoring practices, conducting safety audits, reporting hazards, and ensuring compliance with facility waste management plans. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T15#GNS122_U3_T15_h8)
